findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false; logic is misleading
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions negates the feature flag check and then returns false in both branches, so the flag has no effect. Disabling the feature is intentional, but the code reads as if the flag gates it. A future maintainer who 'fixes' the inverted negation could re-enable the DuckDB path without noticing. Replace this with a plain `return false` and a comment explaining the security reason.

findings.title: Error message misleading for SQL expressions
findings.body: Users receive "sqlExpressions is not implemented", even when the sqlExpressions feature flag is on. In reality the feature was implemented and then deliberately disabled for security reasons. A clearer message such as "SQL expressions are disabled" would tell users that turning on the flag will not help.

findings.title: Existing SQL parser/command tests now fail against the stub DB
findings.body: TablesList now calls the stub DB, whose RunCommands always returns "not implemented". The other legacy SQL path, UnmarshalSQLCommand, calls NewSQLCommand and so fails the same way. Any existing tests that parse SQL table lists or execute SQL commands will fail. The PR does not update or skip those tests and adds no test asserting that SQL expressions are rejected.
